assumptions.name: beta
assumptions.justification: Audit policy: the proposed 0.274425154425 lies outside the 0.3-2.0 band; amended to the nearest bound by the operator's standing policy.

assumptions.name: capex_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of capital expenditure over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2021-12-31, 2022-12-31, 2023-12-31, 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31. The individual observations were 0.0292, 0.0246, 0.0297, 0.0356, 0.0478.

assumptions.name: depreciation_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of depreciation and amortisation over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2021-12-31, 2022-12-31, 2023-12-31, 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31. The individual observations were 0.1745, 0.1236, 0.1017, 0.0873, 0.0866.

assumptions.name: ebit_margin
assumptions.justification: The mean of operating income over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2021-12-31, 2022-12-31, 2023-12-31, 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31. The individual observations were 0.0282, 0.0847, 0.1788, 0.1850, 0.2340.

assumptions.name: equity_risk_premium
assumptions.justification: 4.5 %: inside the 4-6 % band the operator's audit policy accepts, and the neighbourhood of the implied US premium in the Damodaran monthly series through 2026. A judgement, stated as one.

assumptions.name: exit_multiple
assumptions.justification: No peer multiple facts were supplied to me, so this rests partly on convention for large-cap diversified pharma — the operator should know that. It is anchored to the derived economics rather than picked flat: EBIT margin averages 14.2% but is rising (23.4% in FY2025), and D&A intensity (0.1147) far exceeds capex (0.0334), so EBITDA is large relative to EBIT and a mid-range multiple is the conservative read. That D&A-capex gap reflects amortised acquired intangibles that must be replenished by M&A, which a DCF's perpetuity treats as free cash. For that reason I regard this exit multiple as the better terminal anchor than the growth perpetuity, which would imply a materially higher figure. Raise toward 12x if margin expansion proves durable.

assumptions.name: revenue_growth
assumptions.justification: The compound annual growth rate of revenue from 2021-12-31 to 2025-12-31, over 4 year(s): revenue moved from 37,417,000,000 to 58,739,000,000. Held flat across the forecast, because a trailing rate is one number and projecting a fade is a judgement this derivation does not make.

assumptions.name: risk_free_rate
assumptions.justification: The US 10-year Treasury constant maturity yield was 4.94% on 2026-09-17, as published by 2026-09-19 (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.15), series DGS10). Taken as the USD risk-free rate for this run's as-of date and converted to the fraction 0.0494.

assumptions.name: tax_rate
assumptions.justification: Effective tax rate near 20 % (20-F). Stated by the operator because the platform derived nothing for it; recorded as a completeness finding.

assumptions.name: terminal_growth
assumptions.justification: Taken as below a cost of capital of at least 7% (risk-free 4.94% plus any ordinary equity premium for large-cap pharma), so it is safe against any discount rate this run confirms. 2.5% is roughly long-run nominal GDP, appropriate for a diversified portfolio (five therapy areas, dozens of named products, global geographic split) where no single patent expiry is existential, but where US pricing policy and generic erosion cap perpetual real growth. Trailing revenue CAGR of 11.9% is post-Alexion and cannot persist. Lower to ~1.5% if you judge the pipeline replaces less than the LOE base; higher only with evidence of durable pricing power.

assumptions.name: working_capital_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of net working capital — current assets less current liabilities — over revenue, across 5 period(s) ending 2021-12-31, 2022-12-31, 2023-12-31, 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31. A negative figure is normal for a business paid before it pays, and is proposed as it stands rather than floored at zero.
